Merge two BDHS recode files on the right DHS keys

Source: R/merge.R
bdhs_merge.Rd

Detects which recodes x and y are (see bdhs_recodes()) and joins them on the identifiers the DHS Program documents for that pair, so you do not have to remember which line-number variable links a child to its household roster entry. x is the base file: its rows (unit of analysis) and attributes are kept, and the columns of y are added.

Usage

bdhs_merge(
  x,
  y,
  join = c("left", "inner"),
  by = NULL,
  recode_x = NULL,
  recode_y = NULL,
  suffix = NULL
)

Arguments

x, y

Data frames of BDHS recode data (as returned by bdhs_read()). x is the base file.

join

"left" (default) keeps every row of x; "inner" keeps only rows of x with a match in y.

by

Optional explicit key: a named character vector like c(v001 = "hv001", v002 = "hv002") (names in x, values in y), overriding detection.

recode_x, recode_y

Optional recode codes overriding detection.

suffix

Suffix for duplicated column names from y; defaults to "_" followed by the lower-case recode of y (e.g. "_hr").

Value

x with the columns of y added (one row per row of x when y has one row per key), with the attributes of x.

Details

FilesKey (x side = y side)
IR, KR, BR with HRv001, v002 = hv001, hv002
IR with PRv001, v002, v003 = hv001, hv002, hvidx
KR, BR with IRcaseid
KR with BRcaseid, bidx
KR, BR with PRv001, v002, b16 = hv001, hv002, hvidx (child's line number; needs b16)
PR with HRhv001, hv002 (or hhid)
MR with HR / PRmv001, mv002 (, mv003 = hvidx)
HW with KR / PRhwhhid, hwline = household part of caseid, b16 / hhid, hvidx
WI with HR, PR / IR, KR, BRwhhid = hhid / household part of caseid

Both files must come from the same survey round (pooled data are joined within rounds on survey_id). Columns of y that repeat an identifier or design column of x, or that hold exactly the same values as the same-named column of x, are dropped; other duplicated names get the suffix suffix.

The keys follow the DHS Guide to DHS Statistics ("Merging files"). The WI and HW keys for 1993-94 to 2004 follow DHS conventions and could not be verified against the files; check the match rate that is reported.

Examples

kr <- bdhs_simulate(2022, "KR")
hr <- bdhs_simulate(2022, "HR")
kh <- bdhs_merge(kr, hr)
#> ✔ Merged HR into KR on v001, v002 = hv001, hv002: 296 of 296 rows matched
#>   (100%).
table(kh$hv201)
#> 
#>  11  12  21  31  43  71 
#>  14  13 234  13   8  14 

# Mothers' characteristics on the births file
br <- bdhs_simulate(2022, "BR")
ir <- bdhs_simulate(2022, "IR")
nrow(bdhs_merge(br, ir)) == nrow(br)
#> ✔ Merged IR into BR on caseid: 1983 of 1983 rows matched (100%).
#> [1] TRUE
